summary: Sam Witteveen, an AI developer, recaps Microsoft's Windows and Surface event in San Francisco. He focuses on 'hybrid intelligence', where Windows routes tokens between local models and cloud models. In a GitHub Copilot demo, an 'auto' model picker sent simple tasks to a local Microsoft coding model and used a cloud model for planning, with local subagents doing the bulk reading (1.6M tokens, near-zero cost). He also covers heavily quantized local models, llama.cpp inside Windows ML, the MXC agent sandbox with per-agent identity, and the RTX Spark hardware. He is skeptical of the quality of 1-3 bit quantized models and notes that failure handling in the router was not shown.
speakers_or_authors: Sam Witteveen (AI developer, YouTube channel host)
relevance_reason: Useful passage on OS-level agent infrastructure: routing between local and cloud, agent sandboxing and agent identity in Windows. It is mostly developer- and hardware-focused (quantization, runtimes, chips), so only part of it bears on the computer-use agent theme, and it has little on how end users work.

claims.claim: In a demo, a coding agent session sent 1.6 million tokens to a model at zero cost because the model ran on the laptop, and the tool, not the developer, chose to run locally.
claims.quote: it wasn't actually even the developer who decided it should run locally. It was the tool.

claims.claim: The new 'auto' mode in GitHub Copilot can choose a local model as well as cloud models. A simple cleanup task ran locally on the laptop GPU and could continue in airplane mode.
claims.quote: the new version of auto doesn't just choose between cloud models anymore. It can also choose a local model.

claims.claim: For a harder task, a cloud model did the planning and three subagents ran locally on the Microsoft model, so nearly all of the 1.6M input tokens were processed locally (about 150:1 in to out).
claims.quote: The expensive model does the thinking the local cheap models do the bulk reading.

claims.claim: The hybrid routing ships in the GitHub Copilot app on October 15th, with local context, actions and models coming over the following months.
claims.quote: this is going to ship in the GitHub copilot app on October 15th

claims.claim: The demo did not show what happens when the local model fails at a routed task, that is, whether it escalates to the cloud or silently gives a worse answer.
claims.quote: If the local model can't handle the task it was sent, does it then know that and send it back to the cloud

claims.claim: Microsoft showed heavily quantized local models (a 3-bit coding model with a 256k context, a 2-bit Nemotron, and DeepSeek at 1.6 bits). The presenter doubts that quality survives, especially for coding and clean tool calls.
claims.quote: structured output is often the first thing to break when you push quantization too far.

claims.claim: The claim on stage that the 1.6-bit model outperforms on coding and reasoning benchmarks was not clarified.
claims.quote: the claim on stage was that it outperforms on coding and reasoning benchmarks, but they didn't really clarify what that meant.

claims.claim: Windows ML is adding llama.cpp, so open models in GGUF format could be run on day one without Microsoft packaging them. It is unknown whether users can plug their own models into the Copilot router.
claims.quote: the whole idea of llama CPP inside of Windows ML

claims.claim: Microsoft announced Microsoft execution containers (MXC), a runtime sandbox where organizations set policies for agent access and Windows enforces them. Agent actions are attributed to the agent rather than the user, so an agent can be blocked without cutting off the user.
claims.quote: Every action the agent takes is attributed to the agent, not to you.

claims.claim: The RTX Spark Windows laptops offer up to 128GB unified memory and full CUDA support at roughly an RTX 5070 GPU level, with prices starting around $2,600. Rising memory costs push prices higher.
claims.quote: these machines are up to 128 gigs of unified memory, they have full CUDA support

claims.claim: Microsoft's backing marks a step toward local AI becoming the norm, beyond enthusiasts and Nvidia.
claims.quote: having Microsoft joined that bandwagon is definitely a step forward in making all of this the norm rather than the exception.

commercial_interest: No sponsorship is disclosed. The presenter uses Nvidia DGX hardware and DeepSeek models, and says he hopes to get an RTX Spark. The product claims come from Microsoft's own event.
older_event: The event took place the day before the video (October 2026). The Surface Laptop Ultra and Nvidia RTX Spark chip were largely announced in June; the new items are the shipping dates, pricing, the hybrid routing demo, llama.cpp in Windows ML and MXC.
